vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — step-down from July 14 evening's Vibe 5. The July 15 session is defined by a single decisive development: the CENTCOM naval blockade on Iranian ports, reinstated effective approximately 4 PM ET July 15. This event converts three of the July 14 brief's stated Vibe 4 drop criteria from 'absent' to 'confirmed.' First, fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange: CONFIRMED. CENTCOM launched its third consecutive night of strikes against Iran on July 15, targeting military infrastructure at Bushehr, Chah Bahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas — the fourth distinct strike package since July 7. Second, WTI above $76: CONFIRMED. WTI futures closed at $79.34 on July 15, a roughly 3-8% spike from the July 14 $73-77 range, directly reflecting the blockade reinstatement's market signal. Third, MOU breakdown signal: CONFIRMED BY ACTION. The July 14 brief identified three MOU termination instruments to monitor — SNSC formal void declaration, CENTCOM blockade reinstatement, Kharg Island strike. The blockade reinstatement is now confirmed positive. Treasury's concurrent reimposition of Iran oil export sanctions (lifted under the June 19 Islamabad MOU) provides the economic enforcement layer that completes the de facto MOU termination signal. The SNSC void declaration remains absent and Kharg Island has not been struck — suggesting the US is preserving escalatory rungs above the current posture while operationally voiding the MOU's core provisions. The fourth drop criterion — B and O Fire rapid expansion above 5,000 acres with Level 3 evacuation reinstatement — did NOT trigger. The B and O Fire is actually improving: forward progress stopped, acreage holding at 2,815 acres (not expanding), Level 3 evacuations fully downgraded (Level 1 in some areas), and containment holding at 63% through Day 6. This is the session's only significant positive signal and partially mitigates what would otherwise be a clean Vibe 3 scenario. The partial mitigation from the B and O Fire's positive trajectory, Peru JNE credentials smooth completion, and the absence of Kharg Island strike (preserving a de-escalation off-ramp at the highest kinetic threshold) collectively hold the vibe at 4 rather than 3. Dropped from July 14 Vibe 5 to July 15 Vibe 4. Positive factor 1 (B and O Fire forward progress stopped): CONFIRMED — 2,815 acres holding; Level 3 fully downgraded to Level 1/2; Day 6 suppression arc favorable. Positive factor 2 (Peru JNE credentials): SMOOTH — Fujimori/Galarreta/Torres credentialed; Milei attended; July 28 inauguration track confirmed. Positive factor 3 (Kharg Island not struck): STILL ABSENT — highest-kinetic-threshold MOU termination instrument still inactive; de-escalation off-ramp structurally preserved. Negative factor 1 (CENTCOM blockade reinstated): CONFIRMED — MOU de facto terminated by action; naval blockade on Iranian ports active Day 1; one of three terminal instruments now positive. Negative factor 2 (Treasury Iran sanctions reimposed): NEW — Iran oil export sanctions lifted under Islamabad MOU now restored; economic enforcement layer added to blockade action; reversal of MOU's core economic provision. Negative factor 3 (WTI $79.34): ABOVE $76 TRIGGER — war-risk premium now reflects blockade posture rather than MOU-contested ambiguity; Warsh September FOMC deflationary thesis structurally impaired; June CPI's $3.9% positive print now shadowed by July energy price trajectory reversal. Negative factor 4 (60-day nuclear window voided): DE FACTO — nuclear technical talks were never scheduled in 26 MOU days; under active blockade and reimposed sanctions there is no diplomatic architecture in which talks could commence; window expires ~Aug 17 with zero sessions completed. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: CENTCOM blockade lifted and Iran-side restraint confirmed; WTI declining below $76; new diplomatic architecture replacing the defunct MOU. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: Kharg Island strike; direct US-Iran surface engagement in the Strait; Iranian declaration of full Hormuz closure with IRGC enforcement; WTI above $85.

items.summary: July 15 marks the most decisive single-day escalation in the Hormuz arc since the June 19 MOU signing. Three concurrent US actions on July 15 collectively constitute MOU de facto termination. First: CENTCOM reinstated the naval blockade on Iranian ports, effective approximately 4 PM ET. President Trump announced the blockade reinstatement and CENTCOM confirmed execution. The blockade is defined as targeting only Iranian ships or Iran's export customers — stopping Iranian vessels and tankers carrying Iranian crude from entering or leaving Iranian ports — rather than a blanket Strait closure. This is operationally the same posture that preceded the June 19 MOU, reversed in one day. The July 14 brief tracked the CENTCOM blockade as one of three MOU termination instruments (alongside an SNSC formal void declaration and a Kharg Island strike); its confirmation positive as of 4 PM ET July 15 constitutes the brief's operative MOU termination signal. Second: Trump simultaneously abandoned the Strait of Hormuz fee/toll demand that had been floated in the July 13-14 window — under which vessels transiting the Strait would pay a fee for US military protection — apparently concluding that a blockade posture was more operationally coherent than a toll collection framework that faced immediate maritime law objections. The fee abandonment while maintaining the blockade reflects a decision to prioritize enforcement over revenue extraction. Third: The US Treasury Department reimposed sanctions on Iran's oil exports that had been lifted as part of the June 19 Islamabad MOU. The MOU's economic dimension — suspension of oil export sanctions as an incentive for Iranian compliance with open-Strait provisions — has been formally reversed. Treasury's reimposition effectively removes the economic framework of the MOU simultaneously with CENTCOM's removal of its military-restraint framework. On the kinetic side: CENTCOM launched its third consecutive night of strikes against Iran on July 15, constituting the fourth distinct strike package since July 7. Targets confirmed by CENTCOM include Bushehr, Chah Bahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas — a geographically broader target set than the July 7-8 strikes, hitting Iran's coastal military infrastructure across the Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf approaches to the Strait. No Iranian response has been confirmed through July 15 8 PM PDT, but the IRGC's operational posture following three consecutive nights of US strikes and a reinstated blockade is the primary July 16 intelligence unknown. The Oman dual-corridor proposal — the most structured diplomatic architecture since the MOU signing, advanced through the July 12-13 Araghchi-Albusaidi Muscat meeting — has been effectively overtaken by the blockade reinstatement. The Southern Corridor free-navigation framework cannot function under a CENTCOM blockade posture that targets Iranian-flagged vessels and Iranian-destination tankers in the same waters. The 60-day nuclear window (Days 1-60 of the June 19 MOU; Day 27 was July 15) is now de facto void: zero nuclear technical sessions were scheduled in 27 MOU days, and the active blockade + reimposed sanctions provide no diplomatic architecture under which technical talks could commence. The SNSC formal void declaration remains absent and Kharg Island has not been struck — preserving two escalation rungs above the current US posture. The MOU is terminated by action, not by formal declaration.

items.summary: Seven secondary geopolitical threads on July 15 evening. First: Peru JNE credentials ceremony completed as scheduled. The National Elections Jury delivered presidential and vice-presidential credentials to Keiko Fujimori, First Vice President-elect Luis Fernando Galarreta Velarde, and Second Vice President-elect Miguel Ángel Torres Morales simultaneously at the Gran Teatro Nacional in San Borja, Lima. Argentine President Javier Milei was confirmed in attendance. The ceremony marks the formal beginning of the power transfer process ahead of the July 28 inauguration — the transition arc the brief has tracked since the June electoral outcome now resolves toward the July 28 conclusion. No legal challenge or security incident disrupted the ceremony. The Peru arc — copper and silver resource nationalism premium, economic policy continuity question — is tracking toward normalization on July 28 inauguration confirmation. Second: World Cup 2026 semifinal England vs. Argentina. The match was played tonight at Atlanta. Both teams qualified via extra-time quarterfinal wins on July 12. The winner advances to the Final (~July 19) against the France vs. Spain July 14 winner. NIFC-FIFA co-response Day 18 posture is active at the Atlanta venue. Third: Russia fuel crisis Day 15. Omsk refinery remains 75% offline, refining output at lowest since 2005, nationwide rationing continuing, diesel export ban through July. The IEA's 'unprecedented dual shock' designation — Hormuz + Russia Omsk — is now structurally deepening: the CENTCOM blockade reinstatement re-intensifies the Hormuz supply-side shock component precisely as Russian domestic fuel rationing enters its third week. Warsh's three-condition September FOMC normalization thesis (Hormuz / Omsk / commodity relief) now has all three conditions moving in the wrong direction simultaneously for the first time since July 7. Fourth: ASEAN held an informal meeting in Bangkok with Myanmar's foreign minister — the first direct ASEAN-Myanmar contact in five years, testing Myanmar's potential rehabilitation in the bloc following the post-coup suspension. Fifth: Aspen Security Forum Day 1 (Aspen, Colorado, through July 17). The forum opens amid the Hormuz blockade reinstatement — the geopolitical backdrop that will dominate the forum's national security sessions on days 1-2. Sixth: Lebanon fragile hold Day 30. No Hezbollah mobilization orders through July 15 evening — the post-fourth-exchange assessment window that opened July 15 is the primary Lebanon monitoring arc for the July 16-17 window. Seventh: Colombia T-23 (August 7 inauguration), Venezuela earthquake Day 22 (1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing, Maduro access restricted), DRC Ebola — US citizen in Germany treatment facility, not a domestic case, outbreak spreading beyond Ituri.

items.summary: The WTI futures close at $79.34 on July 15 is the energy market's definitive response to the CENTCOM blockade reinstatement, establishing the highest oil-price level since the brief's tracking began. The $79.34 close represents a roughly 3-8% spike from the July 14 range of $73-77, driven by the 4 PM ET blockade activation and the concurrent Treasury reimposition of Iran oil export sanctions. Both developments remove the MOU's key market assumptions simultaneously: the blockade ends the nominal open-Strait posture that had sustained some oil-market optimism through MOU Day 1-26; the sanctions reimposition removes Iran's roughly 1-1.5 million barrels per day of export capacity from the market again. The $79.34 close crosses the $76 threshold the July 14 brief explicitly identified as the Vibe 4 trigger, and is well above the $72 'normalization floor' the brief has tracked since the ceasefire-era Hormuz reopening. For Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's September FOMC deflationary thesis, the July 15 developments represent the most structurally adverse single-day shift in the 2026 arc. Warsh's June 17 inaugural press conference required three concurrent favorable signals: Hormuz normalization (now reversed — blockade reinstated), Russian refining recovery (still at 60%+ below 2005 levels with no restoration signal), and commodity price relief (WTI now $79.34, the highest of the arc). All three conditions are simultaneously moving in the wrong direction for the first time since July 7. The June CPI's 3.9% YoY print — delivered July 14, the first likely sub-4.0% print in the Hormuz arc — is now structurally overshadowed: July CPI will be measured against energy prices that include blockade-reinstatement oil costs, meaning the June deflationary print may represent the arc's most favorable CPI outcome rather than the beginning of a disinflation trend. CME FedWatch September rate hike probability had been expected to shift from 61% toward 40-50% on the June CPI print. The July 15 blockade reinstatement is expected to push probability back toward 55-65% or higher, effectively absorbing and reversing the CPI's deflationary signal. The 30-year Treasury yield and S&P 500 response to the blockade reinstatement in tomorrow's (July 16) pre-market session will be the primary fixed-income and equity market confirmation of the market's updated Warsh September assessment.

items.summary: Five secondary economic-legislative threads on July 15 evening. First: Section 301 tariff completion deadline T-5 (July 20). No White House finalization of the Section 301 successor framework has been announced through July 15 evening. USTR intends to finalize the forced-labor Section 301 framework before the Section 122 emergency tariff authority expires on July 24, creating a 3-4 day gap risk window between the July 20 Section 301 target completion date and the July 24 Section 122 expiry. The proposed architecture (12.5% on 46 countries; 10% on 15 partners including EU, Canada, UK, Mexico) represents a permanent no-cap, no-time-limit replacement for the 150-day Section 122 bridge. With the blockade reinstatement dominating the July 15 policy bandwidth, Section 301 finalization has received no announced presidential attention. Second: FERC AI 30-day informational report deadline is July 18 (nominal; generation adequacy reports officially due July 20 given the Saturday deadline). PNW Climate Week Day 3 is today — the forum is inside its final FERC submission window. ISO/RTOs (PJM/MISO/SPP/CAISO/ISO-NE/NYISO) have three days to the nominal deadline and five days to the generation adequacy report deadline. The July 18-20 window is the first formal public accounting of whether national grid operators can accommodate data center load growth — a proceeding that will set the grid policy baseline for the next 24-36 months. Third: OBBB Law Day 16. Medicaid work requirements and SNAP healthy-food restrictions in 18 states, zero federal court stays. CBO $3.4 trillion 10-year deficit estimate continues to accumulate. No new OBBB legal or implementation developments July 15. Fourth: SAVE America Reconciliation 3.0 (voter ID through budget reconciliation) — Byrd bath risk continuing; no procedural developments July 15. Trump's refusal to sign legislation without voter ID (as of July 10) remains the operative legislative standoff. Fifth: Maine Democratic Party replacement candidate deadline is July 27 (T-12). No candidate has publicly confirmed entry for the November 2026 race against Sen. Susan Collins. The effective organizing window for a viable Collins-race candidacy is now critically compressed.

items.summary: The July 15 Washington fire session records the B and O Fire's continued suppression progress — the session's single significant positive development in an otherwise escalating geopolitical and economic environment. Forward progress of the fire has been confirmed stopped, with acreage holding at approximately 2,815 acres through Day 6. Containment remains at 63%, unchanged from the Day 5 peak achieved following Level 3 evacuation issuance on July 14. Critically, all Level 3 'Go Now' evacuations have been fully downgraded. Okanogan County Emergency Management has reduced evacuations north of Vic Smith Road to Level 1 'Be Ready' — the lowest formal alert level — indicating the fire's growth arc in that sector is no longer considered an immediate life-safety threat. Other areas (Dry Coulee Road, East Dry Coulee Road, Woods Hill Road, north of 23227 State Route 20, Hope Spring Road, and Okanogan Cemetery Road) remain under Level 2 'Get Set' warnings. The Level 3 → Level 1 progression in the Vic Smith Road corridor within 24 hours of the Level 3 issuance is the strongest single-day suppression signal of the B and O arc — it indicates that Incident Management Team resources, including aerial tankers redeployed from the completed Chelan Hills demobilization, arrested the fire's growth and produced rapid containment progress on the fire's most active perimeter segment. The July 14 brief's Day 5 outcome (large fire confirmed; 4 homes destroyed; initial attack broken) was the worst development of the suppression arc to date. Day 6 reverses the trajectory. The active open questions for Day 7 (July 16): does the 63% containment progress toward 80%+ with no new acreage growth, or does East Cascades Onset Day 18 bring the overnight wind and low humidity that could reactivate the fire's perimeter? analyst_summary: July 15, 2026 evening steps down to Vibe 4 from July 14's Vibe 5 — the CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement on Iranian ports, effective 4 PM ET, constitutes de facto MOU termination by US action. This is the most decisive single development in the Hormuz arc since the June 19 Islamabad MOU signing: the blockade is one of the three MOU termination instruments tracked since Day 1, and its activation on July 15 simultaneously triggered the fourth US-Iran kinetic exchange (third consecutive night of strikes, targeting Bushehr, Chah Bahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas), a Treasury reimposition of Iran oil export sanctions, and a WTI close at $79.34 — crossing the $76 Vibe 4 threshold identified in the July 14 brief. The 60-day nuclear window (Day 27 of 60) is de facto void: zero technical sessions were held in 27 MOU days, and there is no diplomatic architecture under which talks could commence under an active US blockade and reimposed sanctions. Trump's concurrent abandonment of the proposed Hormuz transit fee — a toll on vessels seeking US military escort, briefly floated July 13-14 — suggests a decision to prioritize blockade enforcement over revenue extraction, and reflects a posture that the administration frames as 'holding Iran accountable' for commercial ship attacks during the July 7-11 exchange period. The Oman dual-corridor proposal (Southern free navigation / Northern Iranian approval required), the most structurally sophisticated Hormuz governance framework since the MOU signing, is overtaken by the blockade reinstatement; the Southern Corridor free-transit framework cannot operate under a CENTCOM naval blockade targeting Iranian-destination vessels in the same waters. The session's partial offset is the B and O Fire's Day 6 positive trajectory: forward progress confirmed stopped, Level 3 evacuations fully downgraded (Level 1 in the Vic Smith Road corridor — the fastest-moving sector from July 14 — within 24 hours of the Level 3 issuance), and acreage holding at 2,815 acres with no new significant growth. The Chelan Hills demobilization resource redeployment hypothesis from the July 13-14 brief appears confirmed: IMT suppression assets freed from Chelan Hills (demobilized July 13) produced rapid and effective containment progress at B and O on Days 5-6. The secondary positives — Peru JNE credentials smooth completion (Fujimori/Galarreta/Torres credentialed; Milei present; July 28 inauguration confirmed), Lebanon fragile hold Day 30 (no Hezbollah mobilization through July 15 evening), and the absence of Kharg Island strike (two MOU termination instruments still inactive, preserving kinetic escalation rungs) — collectively hold the vibe at 4 rather than 3. Primary watchitems for July 16-17: first, Iranian response posture — does Iran respond to the blockade reinstatement with a naval challenge to CENTCOM enforcement, an IRGC proxy escalation order, or a diplomatic channel activation? The 24-48 hours following blockade activation are the critical response window; second, WTI trajectory following blockade confirmation — does the $79.34 close hold or continue to rise toward the $85 Vibe 3 trigger? Any Iranian naval interdiction or IRGC response that disrupts transit flow would be the catalyst; third, B and O Fire Day 7 containment — does the 63% containment advance toward 80%+ or does East Cascades Onset Day 19 reactivate the perimeter?
